name: TerraTales
tagline: Mother Earth meets her children North, South and Neutral every five years to compare climate notes — then you play, and see the forecast if nothing changes.
problem: Climate data is freely available but hard for most people to understand or connect to their own choices.
solution: A website built on NASA's U.S. Greenhouse Gas Center data: illustrated stories for Brazil, Egypt and Germany with charts and native-language narration, an interactive game where eco-friendly choices change the story, and a forecast section driven by a CNN-LSTM model on air-sea CO₂ flux maps and a regression on population density.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Won the award for most creatively communicating the potential of open data through storytelling.
Shared stories of how climate change affects Egypt, Brazil and Germany, with an AI climate forecasting model and an interactive game for eco-friendly choices.
Three layers by design: story to engage, game to show individual impact, forecast to warn — because 'storytelling alone isn't enough'.
Each country is narrated in its own language (Egyptian Arabic for Egypt), tying the global story to the local event's audience.

lessons: Give data a cast of characters; a family meeting frame makes three countries comparable at a glance.
Pair the story with one thing the audience does and one consequence they see.

sources.note: Team-written story concept, components, models, AI-use disclosure (ChatGPT, Leonardo AI, Canva).
